1→# VonixGuardian → Hytale port — authoritative contract

Status: **CONTRACT FROZEN** (candidate phase). Parent = Hermes (Venix). Workers implement only.

## 1. Pin

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Repo | `Vonix-Network/VonixGuardian` (private) |
10→| Base commit (port base) | `81a4bdb2f7582b12dc988e99b8b245b5c6c183b6` (`main`, version `2.2.1`) |
| Port tree (canonical) | `C:\Users\Pargon\DEV\vonixguardian-hytale` |
| New module | `hytale/` (module path `:hytale`) |
| Build profile | `-PbuildProfile=hytale` |
| Toolchain | **JDK 25** (`C:/Users/Pargon/AppData/Local/Programs/Eclipse Adoptium/jdk-25.0.4.101-hotspot`) |
| Gradle | **9.2.0** (`C:/Users/Pargon/DEV/_hytale-deps/tools/gradle-9.2.0/bin/gradle`). The repo wrapper (8.10.2) MUST NOT be used for this lane. |
| Hytale server API | `com.hypixel.hytale:Server:0.7.4` from `https://maven.hytale.com/release` (published: 0.5.10, 0.6.9, 0.7.2, 0.7.3, 0.7.4) |
| API jar on disk | `C:/Users/Pargon/DEV/_hytale-deps/Server-0.7.4.jar` (112 MB, 38 439 classes, not obfuscated) |
| API signature dumps | `docs/hytale-api/*.txt` (`javap -p` output — read these, do not re-derive) |

20→Engine (`core/`) is shared and **unchanged**: 137 files, zero real `net.minecraft.*` imports, Java 17 bytecode.

## 2. Verified Hytale API facts (from the 0.7.4 jar, not from blogs)

Plugin surface — `com.hypixel.hytale.server.core.plugin`:
- `JavaPlugin(JavaPluginInit init)`; abstract `PluginType getType()` is already final in `JavaPlugin`.
- Lifecycle hooks: `protected void setup()`, `protected void start()`, `protected void shutdown()`. (`setup0/start0/shutdown0` are the final internal wrappers — never override those.)
- From `PluginBase`: `getLogger()` → `HytaleLogger`, `getDataDirectory()` → `Path`, `getEventRegistry()`, `getCommandRegistry()`, `getChunkStoreRegistry()`, `getEntityStoreRegistry()`, `getTaskRegistry()`, `getBasePermission()`, `getManifest()`, `getState()`.
- `HytaleLogger` extends Google flogger: use `getLogger().at(java.util.logging.Level.INFO).log("fmt %s", arg)`.

30→Manifest — `manifest.json` at jar root, keys decoded from `PluginManifest.CODEC` constants:
`Group`, `Name`, `Version`, `Description`, `Authors[] {Name,Email,Url}`, `Website`, `Main` (FQCN), `ServerVersion` (SemverRange; `"*"` = wildcard), `Dependencies`, `OptionalDependencies`, `LoadBefore`, `SubPlugins`, `DisabledByDefault`, `IncludesAssetPack`.
Authoritative reference manifest: `hytale/src/main/resources/manifest.json`.

Events — `com.hypixel.hytale.server.core.event.events.ecs`:
- `BreakBlockEvent` (`getTargetBlock(): org.joml.Vector3i`, `getBlockType(): BlockType`, `getItemInHand()`), `PlaceBlockEvent` (`getTargetBlock()`, `getRotation(): RotationTuple`), `DamageBlockEvent`, `EnvironmentBreakBlockEvent`, `UseBlockEvent`.
- All extend `com.hypixel.hytale.component.system.CancellableEcsEvent`.
- **Verified**: `getEventRegistry().register(BreakBlockEvent.class, consumer)` compiles and is the registered path used by the scaffold.

ECS — `com.hypixel.hytale.component`: `Store`, `ComponentType`, `Component`, `Ref`, `CommandBuffer`, `Holder`, `Resource`, `ArchetypeChunk`. System bases: `com.hypixel.hytale.component.system.{System, EntityEventSystem, EcsEvent, CancellableEcsEvent, RefSystem, HolderSystem}`.
40→
World / blocks:
- `com.hypixel.hytale.server.core.universe.world.World`: `execute(Runnable)` (server-thread hop), `getChunkStore()`, `getChunkLighting()`. There is **no** `setBlock`/`getBlock` on `World` — block I/O lives in `com.hypixel.hytale.server.core.universe.world.chunk.*` (`WorldChunk`, `BlockChunk`, `BlockOperations`, `ChunkColumn`, `BlockComponentChunk`, `AbstractCachedAccessor`, `CachedAccessor`) plus `com.hypixel.hytale.math.util.ChunkUtil`. Cell C2 owns discovering the exact read/write/rotation/extra-data signatures from the jar.
- `BlockType`: `com.hypixel.hytale.server.core.asset.type.blocktype.config.BlockType` (dump: `docs/hytale-api/BlockType.txt`, 498 lines).
- `RotationTuple`: `...blocktype.config.RotationTuple`.

Players:
- `com.hypixel.hytale.server.core.universe.PlayerRef` implements `CommandSender` and `PermissionHolder`: `getUuid()`, `getUsername()`, `hasPermission(String)`, `senderAsPlayerRef()` on `CommandContext`.

Commands: `com.hypixel.hytale.server.core.command.system.{AbstractCommand, CommandContext, CommandRegistry, CommandSender}`; `CommandContext.sendMessage(com.hypixel.hytale.server.core.Message)`; arguments via `...command.system.arguments.system.{RequiredArg, OptionalArg, Argument}`.
50→
Server jar bundles gson (`com/google/gson`, 212 classes). It does **not** bundle slf4j or HikariCP — those are bundled by `:hytale` (see `hytale/build.gradle`).

## 3. Core SPI every cell must obey (do NOT modify `core/`)

- `Guardian.boot(GuardianConfig config, Path dataDir, WorldMutator mutator, OpLevelFallback opLookup, Executor mainThreadExec, ThreadFactory tf)`.
- `Guardian` facade accessors: `config()`, `dao()`, `queue()`, `gate()`, `perms()`, `rollbackEngine()`, `purgeEngine()`, `undoStack()`, `theme()`, `autoPurgeScheduler()`, `perWorldStore()`, `blacklistHook()`, `submitter()`, `api()`, `submit(Action)`, `submitAccepted(Action)`, `awaitQueueDrained(long)`, `close()`.
- Capture helpers on `Guardian`: `submitBlockBreak`, `submitBlockPlace`, `submitContainerChange`, `submitItemDrop`, `submitItemPickup`, `submitEntityKill`, `submitExplosion`, `submitPortalCreate` (see `Guardian.java` 1029-1110 for exact parameter lists).
- Rollback write path: `network.vonix.guardian.core.rollback.WorldMutator` — implement `trySetBlock(...)`, `trySetBlock(..., blockState, blockEntityNbt)`, `tryGiveOrDrop(...)`, plus the clear-to-air path. All called on the server thread.
- Action construction: `network.vonix.guardian.core.action.ActionBuilder` (fluent: `type`, `actorUuid`, `actorName`, `worldId`, `position`, `targetId`, `targetMeta`, `amount`, `oldBlockState`, `newBlockState`, `blockEntityNbt`, `build()`).
60→- Reference implementations to mirror (read before writing): `mc-26.3/fabric/src/main/java/network/vonix/guardian/mc/v26_3/fabric/{FabricBootstrap,FabricEvents,FabricWorldMutator,FabricOpLookup}.java` and `mc-26.3/common/.../{GuardianCommands,Inspector,LookupFormatter,ChatRenderer,WorldKey,SourceTagger}.java`.

Port-local SPI (frozen, owned by the parent, in `hytale/src/main/java/network/vonix/guardian/hytale/spi/`): `GuardianServices`, `WorldBlockAccess`, `BlockSnapshot`, `PlayerDirectory`. Nobody edits `spi/` — if a signature is genuinely wrong, report `PREMISE_BROKEN` with evidence instead of changing it.

## 4. Cell ownership (disjoint paths — never write outside your cell)

| Cell | Package root (under `hytale/src/main/java/network/vonix/guardian/hytale/`) | Mission | May read |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 capture | `capture/` | Hytale events → core `Action`s: player block break/place, environment break, damage/fire/explosion attribution where the API exposes a causer, entity kill, container use. Idempotent, no double-logging, respects `Guardian.gate()`. | `core/`, `mc-26.3/**`, `docs/hytale-api/` |
| C2 worldio | `world/` | Implement `spi/WorldBlockAccess` + core `WorldMutator` for Hytale: read `BlockType` id + rotation + component data at a position, write it back, chunk load/unload handling, world-id ↔ Hytale world UUID mapping, clear-to-air semantics. | same |
70→| C3 commands | `command/` | `/guardian` command tree (`status`, `inspect`, `lookup`, `rollback`, `restore`, `purge`, `undo`, `reload`, `help`) using only `GuardianServices` + core engines; permission gates via `PlayerDirectory`/`Guardian.getBasePermission()`; message formatting via `Message`. | same |
| C4 platform | `platform/` | Bootstrap plumbing: config load (`ConfigLoader`) into the Hytale data dir, `OpLevelFallback` impl from Hytale permissions, `PlayerDirectory` impl, SLF4J→`HytaleLogger` bridge/provider, writer `ThreadFactory`, server-thread `Executor` from `World#execute`. | same |
| C5 bootstrap | `VonixGuardianPlugin.java` (parent) | Lifecycle wiring of C1–C4, `Guardian.boot`, shutdown drain. Written by the parent after C1–C4 land. | all |

**Forbidden for every cell**: `core/**`, `settings.gradle`, `build.gradle` (root or `hytale/`), `hytale/src/main/resources/manifest.json`, `spi/**`, `mc-*/**`, `docs/**`, `.github/**`, git commits/pushes, any `gradle`/`gradlew` invocation, any network call, any deploy/publish.

## 5. Gates

1. **Per-cell compile gate** (workers run this, it writes only to their own output dir):
   ```bash
80→   bash scripts/hytale-compile-check.sh <your-package-dir> [...]
   ```
   It compiles against the real Hytale jar + the prebuilt bundled classpath. Zero errors required.
2. **Parent build gate** (Hermes only): `gradle :hytale:build -PbuildProfile=hytale` → fat jar + no test failures.
3. **Plugin-load gate**: `PLUGIN_LOAD_UNVERIFIED` until a licensed Hytale server install with `Assets.zip` exists on a host we control. Do not claim the plugin loads.

## 6. Output contract (every worker writes this to disk)

```text
STATUS=CANDIDATE_COMPLETE|BLOCKED|NEEDS_ESCALATION|FAILED
90→CANDIDATE=<changed paths + file count>
EVIDENCE=<compile command + result, API signatures you verified from the jar>
PREMISES=<OK | list of brief premises that did not hold, with the real signature>
GAPS=<what is not implemented/proven>
EFFECTS=NOT_PERFORMED
```

Write it to `docs/hytale/results/<cell>.md` (that path is the ONLY file outside your cell you may create).

1→# VonixGuardian — Permission Reference

VonixGuardian v1.0.0 — complete permission node reference.

## 1. Overview

VonixGuardian gates every `/vg` subcommand behind a permission node of the form
`vonixguardian.command.<sub>` (e.g. `vonixguardian.command.rollback`). The
permission prefix is declared in `CommandSpec.PERMISSION_PREFIX` and is
10→identical across every supported loader (Forge, NeoForge, Fabric) and every
supported Minecraft version (1.18.2, 1.19.2, 1.20.1, 1.21.1).

Resolution happens through `network.vonix.guardian.core.perms.PermissionResolver`:

1. **LuckPerms (preferred).** If `permissions.useLuckPerms` is `true` *and*
   LuckPerms is on the classpath, the check is delegated to LuckPerms through
   `LuckPermsBridge` — a **pure-reflection** bridge that never `import`s
   `net.luckperms.*`. LuckPerms is therefore a **soft dependency**: VonixGuardian
   compiles, ships, and runs without it. Detection is performed once per JVM via
20→   `Class.forName("net.luckperms.api.LuckPermsProvider")` and cached as a
   tri-state (`null`/unprobed, `TRUE`/available, `FALSE`/permanently absent).
   `IllegalStateException` (LP loaded but not yet registered during early boot)
   is *not* cached — the next call re-probes.

2. **Op-level fallback.** If LuckPerms is disabled in config, missing from the
   classpath, or returns `UNDEFINED`, the resolver consults the loader-supplied
   `OpLevelFallback` and grants iff `opLevel >= permissions.defaultOpLevel`.
   The default `defaultOpLevel` is `3`, i.e. server-op level 3 (the standard
   "op" tier). Without LuckPerms there is **no granular control** — any
30→   sufficiently opped player can run every `/vg` subcommand.

The console (server source) is always treated as fully authorised by the
loader command layer.

## 2. Permission node table

Every node is a literal string. The first ten are emitted by `CommandSpec` and
are checked by the loader's brigadier tree (`GuardianCommands#register`). The
last two — `bypass` and `viewothers` — are gates queried inside the action
40→pipeline and the lookup/rollback handlers respectively, not on the command
node itself.

| Node                              | Gates                                          | Description |
|-----------------------------------|------------------------------------------------|-------------|
| `vonixguardian.command.use`       | the `/vg` and `/guardian` root literal         | Required to even see the command in tab-complete. Held implicitly by anyone holding any subcommand node in practice, but checked first on the root brigadier node. |
| `vonixguardian.command.inspect`   | `/vg inspect` (alias `/vg i`)                  | Toggle inspection mode; left-/right-click a block to query its history. |
| `vonixguardian.command.lookup`    | `/vg lookup <filter…>`, `/vg near` (alias `n`) | Query the audit log with filter tokens (`u:` `t:` `r:` `a:` `i:` `e:` `#…`); `near` is a small-radius shorthand. |
| `vonixguardian.command.rollback`  | `/vg rollback <filter…>` (alias `rb`), `/vg undo` | Undo matching logged actions. `/vg undo` reverses *your own* last rollback/restore and is gated by the same node. |
| `vonixguardian.command.restore`   | `/vg restore <filter…>` (alias `rs`)           | Re-apply actions previously undone by `/vg rollback`. |
50→| `vonixguardian.command.purge`     | `/vg purge <time>`                             | **Destructive.** Permanently deletes audit rows older than the given duration. Cannot be undone. |
| `vonixguardian.command.near`      | `/vg near` (alias `n`)                         | Listed by `CommandSpec` for completeness. The loader command tree currently shares the `lookup` node for `near`; if you grant `lookup` you grant `near`. |
| `vonixguardian.command.undo`      | `/vg undo`                                     | Listed by `CommandSpec`. The loader tree gates `undo` under `rollback`; grant `rollback` to allow `undo`. |
| `vonixguardian.command.status`    | `/vg status`                                   | Show queue depth, DB health, schema version, mod/MC/loader version. Read-only. |
| `vonixguardian.command.reload`    | `/vg reload`                                   | Reload `config/vonixguardian/config.json` from disk. Some fields (`database.type`, `queue.maxSize`) require a server restart and are reported as `requires restart`. |
| `vonixguardian.command.bypass`    | the action-logging pipeline                    | **Actions performed by holders of this node are NOT written to the audit log.** Not gating any subcommand — it suppresses logging at the source. See § 5. |
| `vonixguardian.command.viewothers`| `/vg lookup` and `/vg rollback` filter scoping | Allows targeting other users without an explicit `u:<name>` filter token. Without it, queries are auto-scoped to the executor. See § 6. |

> The node strings in this table are the same verbatim strings hard-coded in
> the loader command modules
60→> (`mc-<ver>/<loader>/.../common/GuardianCommands.java`) and listed in
> `docs/USAGE.md` § "LuckPerms integration". They are part of the v1.0.0
> public contract — changing them is a breaking change.

## 3. Permission group example (LuckPerms)

A typical two-tier setup: **moderators** can investigate and inspect but cannot
mutate the world or wipe data; **admins** get the full kit.

```text
70→# Moderator — read-only investigation
/lp group moderator permission set vonixguardian.command.use         true
/lp group moderator permission set vonixguardian.command.inspect     true
/lp group moderator permission set vonixguardian.command.lookup      true
/lp group moderator permission set vonixguardian.command.near        true
/lp group moderator permission set vonixguardian.command.status      true
/lp group moderator permission set vonixguardian.command.viewothers  true

# Admin — inherits moderator + mutation + maintenance
/lp group admin parent add moderator
80→/lp group admin permission set vonixguardian.command.rollback        true
/lp group admin permission set vonixguardian.command.restore         true
/lp group admin permission set vonixguardian.command.undo            true
/lp group admin permission set vonixguardian.command.purge           true
/lp group admin permission set vonixguardian.command.reload          true
```

Notes:

- Do **not** grant `vonixguardian.command.bypass` to a human role. It is
90→  intended for the server console and trusted automation only (see § 5).
- `vonixguardian.command.viewothers` is what lets a moderator look up
  *anyone's* edits in a region without typing `u:<name>` for every query.
  Without it, `/vg lookup r:20` only returns the moderator's own actions
  (see § 6).
- The `use` node is what gates the root `/vg` literal — granting only a
  subcommand node without `use` will hide the command from tab-completion on
  some loaders. Always grant `use` to any role that holds any other VG node.

## 4. Fallback when LuckPerms is absent
100→
When LuckPerms is not on the classpath, or when `permissions.useLuckPerms` is
explicitly set to `false` in `config/vonixguardian/config.json`, the resolver
falls back to vanilla op level. The relevant config record is
`GuardianConfig.Permissions(boolean useLuckPerms, int defaultOpLevel)`.

```jsonc
{
  "permissions": {
    "useLuckPerms": true,   // try LP first; harmless if LP isn't installed
110→    "defaultOpLevel": 3     // [0, 4] — 3 == standard server op
  }
}
```

Semantics:

- `defaultOpLevel` is validated by `ConfigLoader` to lie in `[0, 4]`; values
  outside that range reject the config with
  `permissions.defaultOpLevel: must be in [0,4]`.
120→- The default `3` matches the vanilla "op" tier (level 3 is the default for
  `/op <player>` on most servers).
- Holders of an op level `>= defaultOpLevel` are granted **every** VG node
  unconditionally — including `bypass` and `viewothers`. There is no granular
  control without LuckPerms.
- The console always passes because the loader command layer short-circuits
  permission checks for non-player sources.
- An exception thrown by the loader-supplied `OpLevelFallback` causes a
  **deny** (logged at WARN) — fail-closed.

130→If you need per-command control without running LuckPerms, you must run a
permission mod. Pterodactyl- or panel-managed servers can install LuckPerms
side-by-side with VonixGuardian — VG will pick it up automatically on next
reload.

## 5. `vonixguardian.command.bypass` semantics

Holders of `vonixguardian.command.bypass` produce world mutations that are
**never written to the audit log.** This is enforced inside the action
pipeline — the event sentinels query the resolver and short-circuit
140→`EventSubmitter.submit(...)` when the actor has the node.

⚠️ **Security implications.** This node defeats the entire audit chain for the
holder. A griefer who somehow obtained it could destroy your world *and there
would be no record to roll back from*. Therefore:

- **Do not grant `bypass` to a human role.** Not moderator, not admin, not
  even owner.
- Reasonable use cases are limited to:
  - The server console / automation accounts that generate large volumes of
150→    procedural world edits (e.g. WorldEdit replays, scripted regeneration)
    where logging would balloon the database without adding investigative
    value.
  - Trusted bots performing scheduled tasks (e.g. arena resets) where the
    actions are already audited elsewhere.
- If you grant `bypass`, document *why* and *to whom* externally. The audit
  log itself cannot tell you who the bypassed actor was, by design.

## 6. `vonixguardian.command.viewothers` semantics

160→`viewothers` controls **filter scoping** on `/vg lookup`, `/vg near`, and
`/vg rollback`/`/vg restore`. It does *not* gate the subcommand — you also
need the corresponding `lookup` or `rollback` node.

Behaviour:

- **Without `viewothers`:** if the executor does **not** supply an explicit
  `u:<name>` filter token, the query is implicitly scoped to the executor's
  own UUID. `/vg lookup r:20` becomes `/vg lookup u:<self> r:20`. The
  executor sees only their own actions in the region. An explicit
170→  `u:someoneelse` is rejected with a permission error.
- **With `viewothers`:** no implicit scoping. `/vg lookup r:20` returns
  *all* actors' actions in the region; `u:<name>` filters work normally for
  any target.

The intent is to let a server hand out `lookup` to regular players (so they
can audit their own builds without staff intervention) while reserving the
ability to investigate other players for trusted staff via `viewothers`.

## See also
180→
- [`docs/USAGE.md`](USAGE.md) — full command reference and filter token grammar.
- [`docs/CONFIG.md`](CONFIG.md) — `permissions.useLuckPerms` and
  `permissions.defaultOpLevel` field reference plus full config schema.
